messages.author: 5d074889c2204101
messages.subject: epistatic interactions
parts:
Hi all and Karl,

I work on the sunflower genome and wanted to detected epistatic interactions between QTLs. I am a bit confuse by what would be the best approach...

Lets consider the exemple 5 from the rqtltour.pdf.

My questions are :

- Is it really necessary to run scanone? You can detected different QTLs, isolate the genotypes at the markers where the peaks are, are re-run scanone using the detected markers as an interactive covariate. You can plot the effect of the different models on the LOD but you do not formally test the interaction, correct?

- from part8 to the end, you run scantwo with permutation and obtain LOD thresholds and pvalues for interacting pairs (LODfv1 and associated pvalue, correct?). Is it really necessary to re-run scan two with the new thresholds (as in Ex. 5 point9) given that the pvalues are already computed in the permutation test ? the rest of the exemple is I believe to get a better estimation of LOD/positions of the QTL, right?

Do these questions make sense?

Any suggestions about some guidelines would be greatly appreciated! I really like R/QTL but it IS time-consuming...

Thanks so much!

Jonathan

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] epistatic interactions
parts:
I don't quite understand your questions.

You shouldn't need to run scantwo() multiple times.

kalr

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] epistatic interactions
parts:
Hi Karl, 

Thanks for your reply and sorry for the confusion. 

My question was regarding the example 5 (Multiple QTL mapping) point 9. I guess I don't have to provide 5 thresholds values if I run scantwo() with permutations, correct?

When looking for interacting loci, I also have little feeling about the difference between 
- running scanone(), detecting a QTL and running scanone() including the marker as  addcovar / intcovar 
- running scantwo() with permutations. 

Maybe I am wring but it sounds to me that these two approaches have similar goals but I obtained different results... which I believe I did something wrong using scanone() but I will work on it....

So, if I look for epistatic interaction between QTLs, should I "just" run scantwo() with lets say 1000 permutations? probably including detected makers (if some are detected) as a  covariate? Otherwise what would be the best approach? 

Thanks for your guidance! 

Jonathan
